78: def validate(reference_key, estimated_key):
79:     """Check that the input annotations to a metric are valid key strings and
80:     throws helpful errors if not.
81: 
82:     Parameters
83:     ----------
84:     reference_key : str
85:         Reference key string.
86:     estimated_key : str
87:         Estimated key string.
88:     """
89:     for key in [reference_key, estimated_key]:
90:         validate_key(key)
91: 
92: 
93: def split_key_string(key):
94:     """Split a key string (of the form, e.g. ``'C# major'``), into a tuple of
95:     ``(key, mode)`` where ``key`` is is an integer representing the semitone
96:     distance from C.
97: 
98:     Parameters
99:     ----------
100:     key : str
101:         String representing a key.
102: 
103:     Returns
104:     -------
105:     key : int
106:         Number of semitones above C.
107:     mode : str
108:         String representing the mode.
109:     """
110:     if key.lower() != "x":
111:         key, mode = key.split()
112:     else:
113:         mode = None
114:     return KEY_TO_SEMITONE[key.lower()], mode
115: 
116: 
117: def weighted_score(reference_key, estimated_key, allow_descending_fifths=False):
118:     """Compute a heuristic score which is weighted according to the
119:     relationship of the reference and estimated key, as follows:
120: 
121:     +------------------------------------------------------+-------+
122:     | Relationship                                         | Score |
123:     +------------------------------------------------------+-------+
124:     | Same key and mode                                    | 1.0   |
125:     +------------------------------------------------------+-------+
126:     | Estimated key is a perfect fifth above reference key | 0.5   |
127:     +------------------------------------------------------+-------+
128:     | Relative major/minor (same key signature)            | 0.3   |
129:     +------------------------------------------------------+-------+
130:     | Parallel major/minor (same key)                      | 0.2   |
131:     +------------------------------------------------------+-------+
132:     | Other                                                | 0.0   |
133:     +------------------------------------------------------+-------+
134: 
135:     When specifying allow_descending_fifths=True, the scoring changes so that
136:     keys that are a perfect fifth above or below the reference key score 0.5
137:     points. This is consistent with the scoring used for MIREX since 2017.
138:     In the future, the default behaviour will change to use the new method by
139:     default.
140: 
141:     Examples
142:     --------
143:     >>> ref_key = mir_eval.io.load_key('ref.txt')
144:     >>> est_key = mir_eval.io.load_key('est.txt')
145:     >>> score = mir_eval.key.weighted_score(ref_key, est_key,
146:     ...                                     allow_descending_fifths=True)
147: 
148:     Parameters
149:     ----------
150:     reference_key : str
151:         Reference key string.
152:     estimated_key : str
153:         Estimated key string.
154:     allow_descending_fifths : bool
155:         Specifies whether to score descending fifth errors or not.
156: 
157:     Returns
158:     -------
159:     score : float
160:         Score representing how closely related the keys are.
161:     """
162:     # Notify users of difference between default behaviour in mir_eval and
163:     # the scoring used by MIREX since 2017
164:     if not allow_descending_fifths:
165:         warnings.warn(
166:             "The selected key scoring method does not match that "
167:             "currently used by MIREX. To use the same method, specify "
168:             "allow_descending_fifths=True. The default behaviour will "
169:             "change to allow_descending_fifths=True in the future."
170:         )
171: 
172:     validate(reference_key, estimated_key)
173:     reference_key, reference_mode = split_key_string(reference_key)
174:     estimated_key, estimated_mode = split_key_string(estimated_key)
175:     # If keys are the same, return 1.
176:     if reference_key == estimated_key and reference_mode == estimated_mode:
177:         return 1.0
178:     # If reference or estimated key are x and they are not the same key
179:     # then the result is 'Other'.
180:     if reference_key is None or estimated_key is None:
181:         return 0.0
182:     # If keys are the same mode and a perfect fifth up (7 semitones)
183:     if estimated_mode == reference_mode and (estimated_key - reference_key) % 12 == 7:
184:         return 0.5
185:     # If keys are the same mode and a perfect fifth down (7 semitones)
186:     if (
187:         allow_descending_fifths
188:         and estimated_mode == reference_mode
189:         and (reference_key - estimated_key) % 12 == 7
190:     ):
191:         return 0.5
192:     # Estimated key is relative minor of reference key (9 semitones)
193:     if (
194:         estimated_mode != reference_mode == "major"
195:         and (estimated_key - reference_key) % 12 == 9
196:     ):
197:         return 0.3
198:     # Estimated key is relative major of reference key (3 semitones)
199:     if (
200:         estimated_mode != reference_mode == "minor"
201:         and (estimated_key - reference_key) % 12 == 3
202:     ):
203:         return 0.3
204:     # If keys are in different modes and parallel (same key name)
205:     if estimated_mode != reference_mode and reference_key == estimated_key:
206:         return 0.2
207:     # Otherwise return 0
208:     return 0.0
209: 
210: 
211: def evaluate(reference_key, estimated_key, allow_descending_fifths=False, **kwargs):
212:     """Compute all metrics for the given reference and estimated annotations.
213: 
214:     Examples
215:     --------
216:     >>> ref_key = mir_eval.io.load_key('reference.txt')
217:     >>> est_key = mir_eval.io.load_key('estimated.txt')
218:     >>> scores = mir_eval.key.evaluate(ref_key, est_key
219:     ...                                allow_descending_fifths=True)
220: 
221:     Parameters
222:     ----------
223:     reference_key : str
224:         Reference key string.
225:     estimated_key : str
226:         Estimated key string.
227:     allow_descending_fifths : bool
228:         Specifies whether to score descending fifth errors or not.
229:     **kwargs
230:         Additional keyword arguments which will be passed to the
231:         appropriate metric or preprocessing functions.
232: 
233:     Returns
